items.q: Which way do magnetic field lines point outside a magnet?
items.correct: From the north pole to the south pole.
items.random_wrong: There are no field lines around a single magnet.
items.why: By convention field lines run N→S outside a magnet; a lone magnet still has a field.

items.correct: No — only iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.
items.misconception: Yes, all metals are attracted to magnets.
items.random_wrong: Only copper and aluminium are magnetic.
items.why: Most metals (copper, aluminium) are not magnetic; the magnetic metals are iron, steel, nickel, cobalt.

items.q: What does the motor effect need?
items.correct: A current in a wire placed within a magnetic field.
items.misconception: A still wire with no current near a magnet.
items.why: The force comes from a current interacting with a field; no current means no motor-effect force (Fleming's left-hand rule).
